name: הוֹתִיר
gloss: he has left over; he has given abundance
summary: Hothir son of Heman, one of David's singers, who drew the twenty-first lot (1Ch 25:4, 28). The name is the hiphil perfect of יָתַר, the form of Isa 1:9, “unless Yahweh of armies הוֹתִיר us a remnant”: “he has left over”, or, as in Deu 28:11, “he has made abound”. It stands among his brothers' names, several of them clauses of praise (Giddalti, Romamti-ezer); scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: The sons of Heman: “… Mallothi, הוֹתִיר, Mahazioth.”
“The twenty-first, לְהוֹתִיר, his sons and his brothers, twelve.”
“Unless Yahweh of armies הוֹתִיר לָנוּ a survivor”: the same form, of Yahweh.
“Yahweh וְהוֹתִרְךָ for good”: the hiphil “make abound”.

note: BDB's j.ef.an also counts Exo 10:15, Isa 1:9 and Jer 44:7, the hiphil verb הוֹתִיר; the word sheet will show this name on those verbs. Whether the subject is God and the sense “he has left a remnant” or “he has given abundance”, scripture does not say.
